interface.title: IRS Survival Explorer (Immune Risk Score survival explorer)
interface.field: Cancer transcriptomics / immuno-oncology biostatistics (RNA-seq differential expression, gene set enrichment, survival analysis)
interface.stage_of_work: Downstream interpretation: turning finished DESeq2 and clusterProfiler GSEA results into a prognostic-score demonstration
interface.what_it_is_for: Build an immune risk score from significant immune DEGs, simulate a patient cohort from the DEA and GSEA effect sizes, then inspect Kaplan-Meier, log-rank and Cox PH results while tuning the significance cut-offs and simulation settings, with volcano, GSEA lollipop and precomputed PPI network views alongside.

data.note: On first load the app read its bundled DEA_Full_Results_macOS.csv and GSEA_Results_Detailed.csv and showed every tab without any upload. I later uploaded the test files: DEA_results_3_samples.csv in the DEA slot (rejected: 'Missing columns: ['symbol']'), DEA_Full_Results_macOS.csv in the GSEA slot (rejected: missing Description/NES/p.adjust/setSize), and then the correct pair, which gave the same results as the bundled data. The patient cohort is simulated, as the app's own banner says. The sidebar was never reset between tasks, so each task's numbers depend on the settings left by the tasks before it; these carried-over settings are stated in each task's specific label.

tree.general: Show how a gene-expression-derived score separates outcomes and how robust that separation is to analysis choices
tree.specific: Explore how the Immune Risk Score (IRS), built from immune DEGs and GSEA effect sizes, separates survival on a simulated cohort, as a method demonstration, and how DEG/GSEA cut-offs and cohort settings change the hazard ratio and log-rank p
